def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law:
## Definition

Fix gravity $g>0$ and a stationary bed $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$. A shallow-water state is a pair $U=(h,m)$ with depth $h\ge0$ and momentum $m\in\mathbb R$. Its admissible wet/dry state set is
$$K=\{(h,m):h>0,\ m\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.$$
For $U\in K$, define velocity by $u=m/h$ when $h>0$ and $u=0$ when $h=0$. Thus a dry state has both $h=0$ and $m=0$. Define the free surface by $\eta=h+b$ and the physical flux by
$$F(U)=\begin{cases}(m,\ m^2/h+gh^2/2),&h>0,\\(0,0),&U=(0,0).\end{cases}$$
For a continuously differentiable bed, the one-dimensional shallow-water balance law is
$$U_t+\partial_xF(U)=(0,-gh\,b_x).$$
The source is evaluated as zero at a dry state.

A discrete lake-at-rest profile with level $\eta_0$ has $m_i=0$ and $h_i+b_i=\eta_0$ in every wet cell; cells with $h_i=0$ are dry and satisfy $b_i\ge\eta_0$.
lem-pe05-strong-l1-limit-preserves-dry-a:
## Statement

Let $h_k\ge0$ almost everywhere on $\mathbb R\times(0,T)$ and suppose $h_k\to h$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Let $u$ be measurable, put $m=hu$ almost everywhere, and suppose $u=0$ almost everywhere on $\{h=0\}$. Then $U=(h,m)$ belongs to the admissible state set $K$ from [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]] almost everywhere. Also, let initial reconstructions $U_k^0=(h_k^0,m_k^0)\in K$ satisfy $m_k^0=h_k^0u_k^0$, $u_k^0=0$ where $h_k^0=0$, and $|u_k^0|\le M_Q$ on each compact spatial interval $Q$ for a constant $M_Q$ independent of $k$. If $U_k^0\to U_0=(h_0,m_0)$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$, then $U_0\in K$ almost everywhere.
prop-pe05-shallow-water-admissible-state:
## Statement

The admissible wet/dry state set $K$ from [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]] is convex.
lem-pe05-hll-depth-flux-decomposition:
## Statement

At a face of the scheme in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]], write $\alpha=a_R$ and $\beta=-a_L$. There are coefficients $p,q\ge0$ such that
$$\widehat F^h=p h_L^*-q h_R^*,\qquad p\le\alpha,\qquad q\le\beta.$$
If $\alpha>0$ and $h_L^*>0$, then $p<\alpha$; if $\beta>0$ and $h_R^*>0$, then $q<\beta$. These statements include the branches where one speed is zero and the all-dry branch.
lem-pe05-hll-dry-face-direction-and-zero:
## Statement

At any face in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]], if the reconstructed right state is dry, then $\widehat F^h\ge0$, and $\widehat F=(0,0)$ whenever $\widehat F^h=0$. If the reconstructed left state is dry, then $\widehat F^h\le0$, and again $\widehat F^h=0$ implies $\widehat F=(0,0)$.
thm-pe05-hydrostatic-reconstruction-is-w:
## Statement

For any discrete bed values, the update of [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]] leaves every lake-at-rest profile of [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]] unchanged, including a wet/dry shoreline with dry cells above the free-surface level.
thm-pe05-hydrostatic-update-preserves-wa:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$ cells form a finite chain, with two admissible ghost states used only to define the boundary faces, or let the cells be periodic. Apply one step of [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]] to states in $K$ from [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]]. If
$$\lambda\big(a_{R,i+1/2}-a_{L,i-1/2}\big)\le1\quad(1\le i\le N),$$
then each updated state remains in $K$. The depth is nonnegative; if it is zero then the momentum is zero. On a finite chain the total water changes by the net boundary discharge, and on a periodic mesh total water is conserved.
lem-pe05-source-quadrature-consistency:
## Statement

Let $b\in C^2(\mathbb R)$, let the uniform cell width be $d>0$, let $x_i$ be the center of cell $i$, and let $0\le h_i^n\le H$ on a fixed compact space-time cylinder. Set $b_i=b(x_i)$, $\delta_{i,+}=(b(x_i+d)-b(x_i))_+$, and $\delta_{i,-}=(b(x_i-d)-b(x_i))_+$. For the source term $S_i^n$ in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]],
$$S_i^n=\left(0,\frac{g}{2d}\left((h_i^n-\delta_{i,+})_+^2-(h_i^n-\delta_{i,-})_+^2\right)\right),$$
there is a constant $C$ depending only on the compact interval, $b$, $g$, and $H$ such that
$$\left|S_i^{(2)}+g h_i b'(x_i)\right|\le C d.$$
For time slabs $J_n=[n\tau,(n+1)\tau)$, define the piecewise-constant source reconstruction $\mathcal S_d(x,t)=S_i^n$ on $[x_i-d/2,x_i+d/2)\times J_n$. Consequently, if the corresponding piecewise-constant depth reconstructions $h_d$ converge strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$ to $h$ and are locally uniformly bounded, then $\mathcal S_d\to(0,-ghb')$ strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}$.
lem-pe05-discrete-weak-identity-with-sou:
## Statement

Let $d,\tau>0$, $I_i=[id,(i+1)d)$, $t_n=n\tau$, and $J_n=[t_n,t_{n+1})$. Suppose vector states and shared face fluxes satisfy
$$d(U_i^{n+1}-U_i^n)+\tau(\widehat F_{i+1/2}^n-\widehat F_{i-1/2}^n)=d\tau S_i^n$$
as in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]]. For $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times(-\infty,T);\mathbb R^2)$ define the space-time cell average
$$\Phi_i^n=\frac1{d\tau}\int_{J_n}\int_{I_i}\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt.$$
Choose $N$ such that $\varphi$ vanishes for $t\ge t_{N-1}$. Then
$$\sum_i d\,U_i^0\cdot\Phi_i^0+\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\sum_i d\,U_i^n\cdot(\Phi_i^n-\Phi_i^{n-1})+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\sum_i\tau\,\widehat F_{i+1/2}^n\cdot(\Phi_{i+1}^n-\Phi_i^n)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\sum_i d\tau\,S_i^n\cdot\Phi_i^n=0.$$
Every sum is finite because the test is compactly supported.
lem-pe05-hll-flux-reconstruction-converg:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $d_k,\tau_k>0$ tend to zero, set $I_i^k=[id_k,(i+1)d_k)$, $x_i^k=(i+\tfrac12)d_k$, $t_n^k=n\tau_k$, and $J_n^k=[t_n^k,t_{n+1}^k)$, and let $b\in C^1(\mathbb R)$ be locally Lipschitz. On each cell-time slab let $h_k,u_k$ be piecewise constant, with $h_k\ge0$, $u_k=0$ when $h_k=0$, and $m_k=h_ku_k$. Suppose $h_k\to h$ and $u_k\to u$ strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$, $u=0$ almost everywhere where $h=0$, and $h_k,|u_k|$ are locally uniformly bounded. Let $\mathcal F_k(x,t)=\widehat F_{i+1/2}^{k,n}$ for $(x,t)\in I_i^k\times J_n^k$, with face flux from [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]] and bed samples $b(x_i^k)$. Then
$$\mathcal F_k\longrightarrow F(h,hu)\quad\text{strongly in }L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R\times(0,T)).$$
The primitive-velocity convergence and uniform velocity bound are included because the assigned wave-speed formula uses $m/h$ on wet states, which is not continuous at a dry state as a function of $(h,m)$ alone.
thm-pe05-strong-limit-satisfies-smooth-b:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $b\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ and consider a sequence of full-line uniform hydrostatic HLL grids from [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]] with widths $d_k\to0$ and time steps $\tau_k\to0$. Set $I_i^k=[id_k,(i+1)d_k)$, $x_i^k=(i+\tfrac12)d_k$, $t_n^k=n\tau_k$, and $J_n^k=[t_n^k,t_{n+1}^k)$, and sample $b_i^k=b(x_i^k)$. On $I_i^k\times J_n^k$, let $\mathcal U_k=(h_k,m_k)$ and $u_k$ be the piecewise-constant state and primitive-velocity reconstructions, with $m_k=h_ku_k$, $u_k=0$ on dry cells, and $U_i^{k,n}\in K$. Define $\mathcal F_k=\widehat F_{i+1/2}^{k,n}$ and $\mathcal S_k=S_i^{k,n}$ on that same slab, using the sampled bed. Assume that on every compact rectangle in $\mathbb R\times[0,T)$, including the initial layer, the depths and velocities are uniformly bounded; that on every compact rectangle in $\mathbb R\times(0,T)$, $h_k\to h$ and $u_k\to u$ strongly in $L^1$ and $m_k\to m=hu$ strongly in $L^1$; that $u=0$ almost everywhere where $h=0$; and that the initial reconstructions converge locally in $L^1$ to $U_0=(h_0,m_0)$. Then $U=(h,m)$ satisfies, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times[0,T);\mathbb R^2)$,
$$\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb R}\left(U\cdot\varphi_t+F(U)\cdot\varphi_x+(0,-ghb_x)\cdot\varphi\right)\,dx\,dt+\int_{\mathbb R}U_0(x)\cdot\varphi(x,0)\,dx=0.$$
Thus the limit is a locally bounded distributional weak solution of the shallow-water balance law in [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]]. Strong convergence, primitive-velocity convergence and the source-quadrature hypotheses are assumptions; this theorem proves no compactness, entropy inequality or convergence rate.
